newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie dlr finding its feet after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie dlr finding its feet after rate cut.

text.p: AUS$ S/Term range *Support *Restnce *RSI-14 *MA-10 *MA-20
*Overnight range roughly US$0.7640/90
*After Friday's one cent-plus fall on the unexpected rate cut, Australian dollar finds some stability above US$0.7650.
*While erosion of rate differential is a negative and is seen keeping pressure on Aussie, shortcovering after Friday's sell off may keep the dollar above US$0.7650
*U.K. and U.S. market holidays expected to keep trade quiet.
The Australian dollar was finding its feet above US$0.7650, stabilising after Friday's heavy fall induced by the surprise interest rate cut but there remained further near term risks to the downside.

Traders said that if the dollar were to weaken further, there were large stop loss orders from US$0.7630, and while there was potential for shortcovering rallies, sellers were expected to cap any upside moves.
By 8.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) the Australian dollar was at US$0.7663/68, down slightly on Friday's local close of US$0.7680/85.
A break through support at US$0.7630 would lead the way open for a re-test of the 1997 lows of US$0.7550 reached in February.

It was speculation that there could be another rate cut that led to those lows, and the fact that Australian rates are now level with the U.S. Fed Funds rate of 5.50 percent meant that the dollar was now more vulnerable to negative news on commodity prices, traders said.
One bright spot for the dollar was that offshore selling after the cut did not take it through any new support levels, despite the expected negative reaction.

The erosion of the yield differential was expected to lead to selling from offshore investors, who traditionally view the dollar as a high yielding currency. In fact, traders said there were buyers of the Australian dollar near its overnight lows.

Westpac Bank's technical anlayst, Peter Pontikas, said the dollar's fall basically finished after the first hour following the cut, and that the lack of offshore follow-through selling suggested there was room for a rise to US$0.7710 or higher.
On the crosses, the dollar was stable against the yen, but was weaker against the mark after a better than expected showing by parties from the left in the French elections.
The Australian dollar opened at 89.00/10 yen, almost unchanged from 88.89/99 late on Friday, and 1.2893/05 marks, almost a full pfenning down on Friday's 1.2987/3000.
The mark was also strengthening against the yen and the U.S. dollar, as the election results raised some questions as to whether France would push ahead with European Union.
Asian trade is expected to be affected by the closure of U.K. and U.S. markets on Monday, with the strengthening mark is expected to be a focus.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
